output.english_question: Under RBI’s UCB (Urban Cooperative Bank) responsible lending directions, for a retail borrower taking a non-business loan, can a bank levy a higher default charge than it would impose on a corporate customer for the same breach?
sub_queries: RBI UCB responsible lending directions default charges penal charges differential for retail vs corporate
UCB responsible lending directions guidelines on penal interest charges for customer default
RBI circular UCB responsible lending penal charges caps discrimination retail corporate same breach
premises: RBI UCB responsible lending directions govern default/penal charges in UCB lending
Retail borrower refers to a non-business (consumer) loan/customer category
Corporate customer refers to non-retail/ corporate category
The question assumes the same breach occurs in both cases (so any difference would be due to customer category or underwriting/product treatment)
